title: Oozing Ethiopian Rice Stew
description: A resinous, chewy lazy‑sunday rice stew that blends Ethiopian shiro with Mediterranean flavors, served in a nigiri‑shaped form.
instructions: Rinse the jasmine rice until the water runs clear, then soak it for 10 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the diced onion until it becomes translucent.
Add the minced garlic to the pot and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and chickpea flour, cooking for 2 minutes to develop a roux-like base.
Pour in the water, then add paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper, and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the mixture thicken, stirring occasionally, for 20 minutes.
While the stew thickens, cook the soaked jasmine rice in a separate pot of salted water until al dente, about 15 minutes, then drain.
Gently fold the cooked rice into the stew, adjusting the consistency with more water if needed.
Let the combined rice and stew sit covered for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Serve scooped portions shaped like nigiri, garnished with a sprinkle of lemon zest.
